title: Complaints Policy
summary: How Silvering defines, handles, escalates and learns from complaints, aligned to the Housing Ombudsman's statutory Complaint Handling Code, including stage 1 and stage 2 timescales and the compensation framework.
author: P012

version_history.change: Rewritten for the statutory Complaint Handling Code (April 2024): 10 working day stage 1 response, single definition of a complaint.
Compensation framework updated; Member Responsible for Complaints named.
Post-RSH inspection review: service request vs complaint guidance, Awaab's Law link, learning log, stage 2 panel option removed.

blocks.p: We want residents to tell us when we get things wrong, and we want to put things right quickly and learn from them. This policy sets out how {{company.fictional_name}} handles complaints. It follows the Housing Ombudsman's **Complaint Handling Code** (the Code), which has been statutory since 1 April 2024. Where this policy and the Code differ, the Code takes priority.

The policy applies to everyone who receives a service from us: tenants, shared owners, leaseholders, people living in our SilverLiving schemes, applicants for housing and members of the public affected by our work. It covers our own staff and anyone acting on our behalf, including contractors such as Brightline Electrical Ltd and Castlemere Construction Ltd.

blocks.quote: An expression of dissatisfaction, however made, about the standard of service, actions or lack of action by the organisation, its own staff, or those acting on its behalf, affecting a resident or group of residents.
blocks.by: Housing Ombudsman Complaint Handling Code, section 1.2

blocks.p: A resident does not have to use the word 'complaint' for it to be treated as one. If a resident expresses dissatisfaction, the person taking the contact must ask whether they want to make a complaint. If they do, it must be logged in Keystone Housing the same day.

A **service request** is a request for us to provide or improve a service, for example reporting a repair for the first time. A service request is not a complaint. However, if a resident is unhappy with how a service request has been handled - for example the repair was not done on time, or a promised call back did not happen - they can complain, and we must not make them wait for the service request to finish before we accept the complaint.

blocks.callout: Damp and mould: a first report of damp or mould is a service request and must go to the Damp & Mould team under Awaab's Law timescales. A complaint about how a damp report was handled must be logged as a complaint as well. Never ask a resident to choose between the two.
blocks.title: Awaab's Law

blocks.h2: 2.2 What this policy does not cover

bullets: Issues that happened more than 12 months before the complaint was made, unless there is a good reason (for example ongoing disrepair or a vulnerable resident). We will consider each case individually and explain any refusal in writing.
Matters that are, or have been, the subject of legal proceedings. Pre-action correspondence alone is not a reason to refuse a complaint.
Insurance claims for personal injury or damage to belongings, which go to our insurer.
Anti-social behaviour reports themselves, which are handled under the ASB Policy. A complaint about how we handled an ASB case is a complaint.
Matters outside our control, such as council tax or housing register decisions taken by the borough council.

blocks.p: If we decide not to accept a complaint we will write to the resident explaining why, and tell them they can ask the Housing Ombudsman to review our decision.

bullets: By phone to the Customer Contact Centre, 8am to 6pm Monday to Friday.
Through the MySilvering app or portal ('Make a complaint').
By email to customerservices@silvering-homes.org.uk.
By letter to Kingsgate House, 14 Fremlin Walk, Maidstone ME14 1QZ.
In person to any member of staff, including operatives and housing officers.
Through a representative, councillor or MP, with the resident's consent.

blocks.p: We will make reasonable adjustments under the Equality Act 2010, for example large-print or audio letters, a phone call instead of a letter, an interpreter or extra time. Adjustments must be recorded on the resident's Keystone record so the next person does not have to ask again.
We have a two-stage process. Timescales are in **working days** and run from the date we receive the complaint (acknowledgement) or the date we acknowledge it (response).

rows: Customer Contact Centre or Complaints Officer
Complaints Officer, with the service manager
Up to 10 further working days, with reasons given to the resident
Within 5 working days of the escalation request
Customer Resolutions Manager or a Head of Service not involved at stage 1
Up to 20 further working days, with reasons given to the resident
table.caption: Table 1: Complaint timescales (Complaint Handling Code sections 5 and 6)

numbered: Log the complaint in Keystone Housing with the category, the resident's desired outcome and any vulnerability or adjustment.
Acknowledge in writing within 5 working days, setting out our understanding of the complaint and the outcome the resident wants. If anything is unclear, ask.
Contact the resident by phone wherever possible. Most complaints are resolved better by a conversation than a letter.
Investigate: check the repairs history in FieldLoop, the contact notes in Keystone and speak to the staff involved.

Respond in writing within 10 working days of acknowledgement using the stage 1 response template. The response must cover every point raised, the decision on each (upheld, partly upheld or not upheld), the reasons, any remedy, any outstanding actions with dates, and how to escalate to stage 2.
Record the outcome, compensation and learning in Keystone.

blocks.p: A resident can ask for stage 2 if they are unhappy with the stage 1 response. They do not have to give reasons, although we will ask what is still unresolved. The stage 2 response is written by someone who was not involved at stage 1. It is our final response, and it must tell the resident how to refer the complaint to the Housing Ombudsman.

Residents can contact the Housing Ombudsman at any time for advice. Once our process is complete, they can ask the Ombudsman to investigate. We co-operate fully with the Ombudsman and comply with orders within the timescales set. The Customer Resolutions Manager reports every determination to the Customer Experience Committee.

Where something has gone wrong we will acknowledge it, apologise, and put it right. Remedies include: doing what should have been done, reviewing a decision, changing a policy or procedure, and financial redress. Compensation is not a substitute for fixing the problem.

rows: One missed appointment; a late letter
Moderate - repeated failure or some distress
Call backs not made over several weeks; repair redone more than once
Serious - significant distress or impact over months
Long-running disrepair; damp and mould not dealt with in Awaab's Law timescales
Director of Customer Experience approval required
table.caption: Table 2: Compensation framework (time, trouble and inconvenience)

bullets: Where a complaint is **upheld** or **partly upheld** because of a service failure, a time and trouble award of at least £50 should normally be made. If no award is made the response must explain why.
Loss of heating or hot water: £5 per day after the first 24 hours (October to April) and £2.50 per day (May to September), in addition to any time and trouble award.
Compensation is paid within 10 working days of acceptance, normally by bank transfer. It is not offset against rent arrears without the resident's written agreement.

blocks.p: Every complaint closed at stage 1 or stage 2 must have a learning entry in Keystone, even if the learning is 'none identified'. The weekly complaints case review looks at open cases, overdue responses and themes. The Customer Experience Committee receives a quarterly complaints performance report, and the Board receives the annual Complaints Performance and Service Improvement Report alongside the Code self-assessment.

rows: Approves the annual self-assessment and service improvement report. The Member Responsible for Complaints (MRC) is the Chair of the Customer Experience Committee.
Owns this policy; approves compensation over £650.
Manages the complaints team; handles stage 2; liaises with the Housing Ombudsman.
Investigate and respond at stage 1; record learning.
Recognises and logs complaints at first contact; acknowledges within 5 working days.
Provide information to complaints officers within 3 working days of a request; deliver remedies on time.

blocks.p: We will only restrict contact with a resident in exceptional circumstances, under our Unacceptable Behaviour Policy. Any restriction must be approved by the Customer Resolutions Manager, explained to the resident in writing, and must not stop them from accessing the complaints process.
This policy is reviewed every year after the annual Code self-assessment, or sooner if the Code or the law changes.

title: Complaint Handling Code Self-Assessment 2025/26
summary: Silvering's annual self-assessment against the Housing Ombudsman's Complaint Handling Code for 2025/26, with a compliance table, evidence and improvement actions; approved by the Board in June 2026.
author: P012

version_history.change: Director review; section 6 changed from 'Compliant' to 'Partially compliant'
Approved by the Board on 24 June 2026; published on the website

blocks.p: The Housing Ombudsman's Complaint Handling Code requires every member landlord to assess itself against the Code each year, publish the result, and submit it to the Ombudsman with the annual Complaints Performance and Service Improvement Report. This self-assessment covers the year 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026. It was scrutinised by the Resident Scrutiny Panel on 4 June 2026 and approved by the Board on 24 June 2026.

The year was a difficult one. The Regulator of Social Housing's inspection in March 2026 graded us **{{fact:rsh_grade}}** and named complaint handling as one of two areas for improvement. Satisfaction with our approach to complaints handling (TP09) was **{{fact:tsm_complaints_2526}}** among renting residents. This self-assessment is honest about where we fall short.

kv: 1 provision (5.8 - learning recorded on every case)
Chair of the Customer Experience Committee

blocks.p: The Resident Scrutiny Panel told us that letters were too long, too formal, and often did not say clearly what we would do next or by when. Residents said call backs promised at stage 1 often did not happen. We have accepted these points and introduced a new plain-English stage 1 template in April 2026.

The Board has reviewed this self-assessment and is satisfied that it is an accurate reflection of our complaint handling. The Board has agreed the improvement actions and will monitor them through the Customer Experience Committee.

summary: Quarterly complaints performance report for July to September 2026 for the Customer Experience Committee: volumes, stage 1 timeliness, categories, outcomes, compensation, stage 2 and Ombudsman cases, and learning.

blocks.p: We received **{{fact:cx_q2_s1_received}}** stage 1 complaints in Q2 (July to September 2026). Only **{{fact:cx_q2_s1_in_target}}** were answered within the Code's 10 working day timescale. This is the lowest quarter since the Code became statutory and is well below our 90% target.

One of three complaints officers was on extended leave in July and August, and complaints about repairs delays rose as routine repairs performance fell (see the Repairs Performance report). September was the worst month, with a backlog of responses waiting for information from the repairs team. October has recovered after the weekly case review was introduced.

title: Resident Scrutiny Panel Review - How We Communicate With Residents
summary: The Resident Scrutiny Panel's review of how Silvering communicates with residents, with evidence from a workshop, mystery shopping and complaints, ten recommendations and the management response.
author: P033

blocks.p: The Panel chose communication because it runs through almost every complaint we read. Satisfaction that Silvering keeps residents informed about things that matter to them (TP07) and that it listens and acts (TP06) are both low, and the regulator's inspection said complaint handling must improve. As one Panel member put it, 'Half the complaints wouldn't exist if someone had just rung back.'

kv: Bernard McDonald, Hollie Frost, Norman Smith, Dawn Turner, Christopher Chan
Grace Osei, Resident Involvement & Insight Officer

bullets: Read 30 anonymised stage 1 complaint files and response letters from 2025/26 and 2026/27.
Ran a resident workshop on 9 September 2026 at Linton Lodge (22 residents, sticky-note exercise).
Mystery-shopped the contact centre: 20 calls at different times, including 5 asking for a call back.
Reviewed the MySilvering app and the letters sent at sign-up, rent increase and repairs appointments.
Interviewed Hannah Lowe (Customer Service Team Leader), Owen Fletcher (Customer Resolutions Manager) and two housing officers.

blocks.p: Of 5 call backs requested in mystery shopping, only 2 happened within the time promised. Advisers were polite and helpful, but there was no reliable way to make sure promised call backs were made. The Panel noticed that the free-text TSM comments repeat the same message.

Stage 1 letters were often long and formal. Twelve of the 30 letters we read did not say clearly what would happen next, or when. Three letters upheld a complaint but offered no compensation and gave no reason why. Several used words like 'remedial', 'escalate' and 'liaise' that residents find off-putting.
Average wait on our mystery calls was just over 6 minutes, and over 15 minutes on Monday mornings. There is no option to book a call at a set time.
Residents are not told when an operative orders a part or when a job passes to a contractor. People then ring to chase, which adds to call waiting times.

rows: Every promised call back is logged as a task in Keystone with a due time
Stage 1 letters use plain English, say what happens next and when, and are no longer than two pages

Any upheld complaint without compensation must say why

author: P030

blocks.p: Use this every time a resident reports a repair by phone, email or in person, and when checking MySilvering reports that look urgent. If you are unsure, **ask the safety questions first** and if still unsure, treat it as an emergency and tell the Repairs Planning team on the Teams channel.

A danger to health, safety or security, or serious damage to the building

blocks.p: Since 27 October 2025 the law sets strict timescales. If a resident reports damp or mould, ask: where is it, how big is it, how long has it been there, is anyone in the home unwell (especially breathing problems), and are there children? Then:

bullets: If the resident or a family member's health is at immediate risk - for example a child with asthma sleeping in a room with extensive black mould - raise an **emergency** and tell the Damp & Mould team straight away. Emergency hazards must be made safe within 24 hours.
All other damp and mould: raise a damp and mould inspection in FieldLoop. The surveyor must investigate within 10 working days.
Never tell a resident it is 'just condensation' or to 'open the windows'. That is a decision for the surveyor after an inspection.
Tell the resident they will get a written summary within 3 working days of the inspection.

blocks.callout: Common mistake: logging 'No heating or hot water' as urgent in winter. In October to April it is always an emergency. Check the month!

blocks.h1: When does it count as a complaint?

blocks.p: If a resident tells you they are unhappy with something we have done, or not done, it is a complaint. They do not have to use the word. Ask: 'Would you like me to log this as a complaint so a complaints officer can look into it?'

Third call about the same tap, two missed appointments
Complaint - log it and rebook the repair
Complaint about communication - log it and arrange the call back
ASB report - pass to the housing officer, not a complaint

numbered: Open the resident's record in Keystone and select New > Complaint.
Choose the category and write the complaint in the resident's own words.
Record what the resident wants to happen (desired outcome).
Tick any vulnerability or adjustment.
Read back your summary to the resident.

blocks.p: Tell the resident that they will receive an acknowledgement within 5 working days and a full response from a complaints officer **within 15 working days**. If they are still unhappy they can ask for their complaint to go to stage 2.

blocks.callout: Do not promise compensation or a particular outcome. That is decided by the complaints officer.

title: Knowledge Article - Taking a Damp and Mould Call
summary: Call script and checklist for advisers taking damp and mould reports under Awaab's Law, including the questions to ask, how to triage emergency hazards and what to promise the resident.
author: P030

blocks.p: Awaab's Law came into force on 27 October 2025. It is named after Awaab Ishak, a two-year-old who died in 2020 from a respiratory condition caused by mould in his home. The way we take the first call decides whether we meet the legal timescales. {{company.fictional_name}} has had {{fact:damp_cases_awaab}} cases within scope of Awaab's Law, and {{fact:damp_breaches}} breached a timescale.

numbered: Where in the home is the damp or mould? (Room, wall, ceiling, around windows)
Roughly how big is it? (Size of a hand, a door, a whole wall)
How long has it been there? Has it come back after being treated?
Is anyone in the household unwell, especially with asthma or breathing problems? Is anyone pregnant, elderly or under five?
Is it near electrics, or is there water coming in?
Is there anything else wrong with the home that worries you?
Can we have photos through MySilvering or by email?

rows: Extensive mould in a room where a child or vulnerable person sleeps, or water near electrics
Emergency - phone the Damp & Mould team on the hotline and raise an emergency in FieldLoop. Make safe within 24 hours; consider temporary moves.
Raise a damp and mould inspection in FieldLoop. Investigation within 10 working days.
Still raise an inspection. Give the 'Keeping your home well ventilated' leaflet as well, not instead.

bullets: A surveyor will investigate within 10 working days (sooner if an emergency).
You will get a written summary of what we found and what we will do within 3 working days of the inspection.
If safety works are needed they will start within 5 working days of the investigation.

blocks.callout: If the resident also says they are unhappy with how we have handled damp before, log a complaint too. Both processes run at the same time.

title: Stage 1 Complaint Response - Letter Template
summary: Plain-English template for stage 1 complaint response letters that meets the Complaint Handling Code: summary, findings, decision per point, apology, remedy, compensation, learning and escalation rights.
author: P012

blocks.callout: Replace everything in [square brackets]. Keep to two pages. Use 'we' and 'you'. Avoid jargon such as 'remedial', 'liaise' and 'escalate'. If you uphold a complaint and do not offer compensation, you must say why.
blocks.title: How to use this template

blocks.p:
[Resident name]
[Address line 1]
[Postcode]

Our reference: [CMP-xxxxx]
Date: [date]
Dear [Mr/Mrs/Ms surname or first name, as the resident prefers],
Thank you for contacting us on [date received] about [one-sentence summary]. I am sorry that you have needed to complain. You told us you would like [desired outcome].
[What you checked: repair history, contact notes, conversations with staff. What happened, in date order. Be honest about what went wrong.]
I have [upheld / partly upheld / not upheld] your complaint. [One line per point raised, with the decision and the reason.]

bullets: [Action] - [who] - [by when]
[Action] - [who] - [by when]

blocks.p: [Compensation: 'In recognition of the time, trouble and inconvenience this has caused, I would like to offer you £[amount].' Or: 'I have not offered compensation because [reason].']
[The change we are making so this does not happen to anyone else.]

If you are unhappy with my response you can ask us to look at your complaint again at stage 2. You do not need to give a reason. Just reply to this letter, email customerservices@silvering-homes.org.uk or call us. We will acknowledge your request within 5 working days and respond within 20 working days of that acknowledgement.

You can also contact the Housing Ombudsman at any time for advice: www.housing-ombudsman.org.uk, 0300 111 3000.

Yours sincerely,

[Name]
[Job title]
Customer Resolutions Team, Silvering Homes

sql: SELECT c.complaint_id, c.complainant, c.scheme_name, c.received_date, c.ack_date, c.stage1_response_date, c.stage1_outcome, c.category, c.summary, c.channel, c.handler, t.address_line1 AS addr, t.postcode AS pc, substr(c.received_date, 1, 4) AS yr, CASE c.handler WHEN 'Mark Pennington' THEN 'P032' ELSE 'P012' END AS author_id, CASE c.handler WHEN 'Owen Fletcher' THEN 'Customer Resolutions Manager' ELSE 'Complaints Officer' END AS handler_title, CASE c.category WHEN 'Repairs - delay' THEN 'I have reviewed the repair history in FieldLoop and the notes on your account. Our records confirm that the operative who attended told you a part had been ordered, but no follow-on job was raised, so the work was never scheduled. This should not have happened, and it meant you waited far longer than our target and had to chase us.' WHEN 'Lettings & transfers' THEN 'I have reviewed the void works record and the notes from your sign-up. The home was marked ready to let before the final clean and safety checks had been completed, and nobody told you about the outstanding work before you collected your keys. Moving home is stressful enough without this.' WHEN 'Staff conduct' THEN 'I have spoken with the officer concerned and their manager, and read the visit notes. I accept that your personal circumstances were discussed where neighbours could hear. That falls short of the confidentiality and respect you are entitled to expect from us.' WHEN 'Communication' THEN 'I have reviewed the contact history on your account. You contacted us several times, and on at least two occasions you were promised a call back that did not happen. The requests were noted on your record but were not set up as tasks, so nobody was prompted to follow them up.' WHEN 'Repairs - quality' THEN 'I have reviewed the job history and the post-inspection notes. The repair was attended three times, and the first two visits did not fix the underlying fault. The quality of those visits was not good enough. I have also found that one appointment was rearranged at your request, which is why I have partly upheld this part of your complaint.' WHEN 'Damp & mould' THEN 'I have reviewed your damp and mould case and the surveyor''s notes. Our surveyor inspected your home, but you were not sent the written summary of the findings and planned works within the 3 working days the law now requires. You were left not knowing what would happen next.' ELSE 'I have reviewed your records and spoken with the staff involved.' END AS finding, CASE WHEN c.compensation_gbp > 0 THEN 'In recognition of the time, trouble and inconvenience this has caused, I would like to offer you £' || c.compensation_gbp || '. Please reply or call us with your bank details and we will pay it within 10 working days. It will not be used to reduce any rent balance unless you ask us to.' ELSE 'We will keep you updated on the actions above.' END AS comp_text, COALESCE(c.learning, 'I have shared your case with the team manager so it can be discussed at the next team meeting.') AS learning_text FROM complaints c LEFT JOIN tenancies t ON t.tenancy_ref = c.tenancy_ref WHERE c.status = 'Closed' AND c.stage1_outcome IN ('Upheld', 'Partly upheld') ORDER BY c.received_date DESC LIMIT 8

title: Handwritten complaint letter - Frank Taylor, 34 Brenchley Gardens
author: P030
summary: Scanned handwritten letter of complaint from Frank Taylor about a boiler repair that was never completed after a gas leak was made safe in July 2026. Logged as CMP-24036.

blocks.hand:
Frank Taylor
34 Brenchley Gardens
Maidstone ME15 8RE

1st September 2026
To the Complaints Department, Silvering Homes

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing because I have given up on the phone. On the 28th July I smelt gas in the kitchen and your engineer came out the same evening and capped the boiler. He was very good. He told me a new part was needed for the boiler and that it had been ordered and someone would ring me within the week.

Nobody has rung. I have called 4 times (5th Aug, 12th Aug, 19th Aug and 27th Aug) and every time I am told there is a note on the system and someone will call me back. Nobody does.

We have had no hot water for over 5 weeks except the kettle. There are four of us here including my grandson who is 7. We have been washing at my daughter's. Summer is nearly over and I am worried about the winter with no heating.

I want the boiler fixed, I want someone to tell me WHEN, and I think we should get something back for all this.

Yours faithfully,

F. Taylor

Tel 07700 900743 (please ring after 10am)
Logged CMP-24036 03/09 - HL. Repairs: no follow-on job found in FieldLoop?

subject: ESCALATION - Colin Vaughan, Flat 120 Brenchley Gardens - no heating, 4th call
summary: Contact centre team leader escalates a vulnerable Brenchley Gardens resident with no heating after a 'parts ordered' visit; Owen Fletcher links it to the same pattern as CMP-24036 and Repairs confirms no follow-on job had been raised.

messages.body:
Hi Owen, Kwame,

I need to escalate this one. Colin Vaughan, Flat 120 Brenchley Gardens (TEN500266), has just called for the fourth time since 26 October. His heating stopped working on the 24th. An operative attended on the 26th and told him a new diverter valve had been ordered. Nobody has been back and nobody has called him.

He has a mobility vulnerability flag, lives with his wife and adult son, and says the flat is 'freezing'. Zainab logged a complaint on 2 November (CMP-24162) - Mark has it - but I'm worried about him now, not in 10 working days.

I've checked FieldLoop and can't see a follow-on job for the part. It looks exactly like Mr Taylor's case at number 34 in September.

Can someone please confirm today when the part will be fitted? He has been offered two oil-filled heaters but they haven't been delivered either.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah,

You're right - the operative closed the job on the 26th as 'parts required' but didn't raise the follow-on. That's the third one at Brenchley in two months. The valve is in stock at Aylesford.

I've raised an emergency job (no heating, vulnerable, November) for tomorrow morning, 8-12 slot, and Lee will deliver two heaters this afternoon on his way past.

Daniel - copying you because we need to fix the 'parts required' close-out in FieldLoop. Operatives shouldn't be able to close without a follow-on job number.

Kwame

Thanks both.

Mark - please ring Mr Vaughan today to confirm the heaters and tomorrow's appointment, and record the call against CMP-24162. When you write the stage 1, use the heating compensation in the policy (£5 a day after the first 24 hours, October to April) on top of time and trouble, and say clearly what we've changed.

I'll add the 'parts required' pattern to Wednesday's case review and to the Q3 report. If we can't stop operatives closing jobs without a follow-on, we'll keep getting these.

Owen

Spoke to Mr Vaughan at 3.50pm. Heaters delivered at 3.15pm. He's grateful but tired of chasing - he asked me to make sure 'it actually happens tomorrow'. I've said I'll call him at 1pm tomorrow to check.

Mark

title: Complaints weekly case review
summary: Weekly complaints case review: responses due in the next 5 working days, two open stage 2 cases, the 'parts ordered' repairs pattern, Ombudsman cases and Q2 performance.
description: Weekly review of every complaint response due in the next 5 working days, stage 2 cases and Ombudsman cases. Started October 2026 as part of the complaints recovery plan.

transcript.text: Morning everyone. Let's give it a sec for Kwame... OK, he's joining from the depot. Right, can everyone see the tracker? I'm sharing the Keystone report.
Yep, got it.
Yes, I can see it. Sorry, there's a bit of background noise, I'm at Kingsgate in the open plan.
No problem. So, responses due in the next five working days. We've got... four on stage 1 and nothing overdue for the first time since June, which, honestly, is a relief.

The lift one at Kings Hill, George Stewart, CMP-24179. That came in yesterday so it's not due till the seventeenth, but the lift's been out three times since August. Liftwise say it's a controller board.
OK. Make sure the acknowledgement goes by the third. And ask Priti's team for the LOLER dates so we're not guessing.
Will do.
And I picked up Rita Turner this morning, Larkfield Close, CMP-24039. Heating again. Operative said parts ordered, and then nothing. She's been without heating eight days.
Sorry - Kwame here, I was on mute. Is that another 'parts ordered'? That's... that's the pattern I was worried about.
It is. Kwame, how many of these do you think there are?

Honestly, I don't know. FieldLoop lets the operative close a job as 'parts required' without raising the follow-on. It's meant to go to the planners to raise, but if it's a busy day it just sits there. I'll run a report on all jobs closed 'parts required' in the last three months with no follow-on.
Please. That would be really useful for the Q3 report too.
I'll have it to you by Friday. And I'll get Rita Turner's part booked today - Larkfield, is that Joel's patch?
Yes, Joel Mensah. I'll let him know.
Thanks. OK, stage 2. Two open. Frank Taylor, Brenchley Gardens, CMP-24036 - the handwritten letter. Stage 2 response due 24 November. Amira, you know him?
I do, yes. Lovely man. He's got his grandson living with him. He was really upset that the stage 1 said not upheld when he'd had no hot water for weeks.

Yeah, I've read it. Between us, I don't think stage 1 was right. The repairs history shows the gas emergency on the twenty-eighth of July, made safe, and then no follow-on job at all for the boiler part. It's the same pattern. And stage 1 went out late as well - eight days late.
That was over the summer when we were two people down.
I know, I'm not blaming anyone. But we need to put it right at stage 2. I'll do it myself. Amira, could you visit him before the twentieth and check the boiler's actually working now?
Yes, I'm on Brenchley on Thursday anyway.

Great. The other one's Rosie Allen at Kings Hill Quarter, CMP-24201, communication. Due first of December. She's also in arrears, I think - Bev's team have her as a hardship referral. Can we make sure income don't send her anything scary while the complaint's open?
I'll flag it to Bev. Ryan Tait's her income officer.

Thanks Hannah. Ombudsman. Three referred and awaiting determination - Kim Hooper at Shepway Green, Dawn Collins at Brenchley, and Rebecca Smith also at Brenchley. Nothing new from the Ombudsman this week. Kim Hooper's the one I'm most worried about: child with asthma, mould kept coming back.
Do we know if Ellie's been back to Kim Hooper's since the works?
Good question. I'll ask Ellie. If it's come back again I want to know before the Ombudsman does.
Themes. Hannah, anything from the contact centre?

Call backs. Same as ever. The Scrutiny Panel report's out and recommendation one is every call back as a Keystone task. We're starting that on Monday. The trouble is, the advisers already have about forty tasks each a day.
I know. But if it's not a task it doesn't happen. Let's try it for a month and see.
Fair enough.

Can I raise one thing? The learning field. Craig's team were supposed to make it mandatory by the end of October. It's still optional. I closed six cases last week and I'll be honest, I left it blank on two.
Ha, thanks for the honesty. I'll chase Craig. That's on the Q2 action list and it'll show as overdue on Monday.

Q2 report went to the Committee pack on Monday. Q2 stage 1 in target was {{fact:cx_q2_s1_in_target}} - lowest quarter we've had. October looks much better, every one so far in time. Rachel's asked for a short paragraph on what's different.
It's this meeting, isn't it. Plus Leah back from leave.
I'll take the credit!
Ha. OK. Anything else? No? Right, thanks everyone, same time next week. Kwame, the report by Friday please.
Will do. Cheers.

recap.summary: Four stage 1 responses due in the next five working days and none overdue. Two open stage 2 cases were reviewed; Owen will write the Frank Taylor stage 2 himself because stage 1 was late and missed that no follow-on boiler job was raised. A recurring 'parts required' pattern in FieldLoop was identified; Kwame will report on affected jobs. Three Ombudsman cases are awaiting determination. Q2 stage 1 in target was {{fact:cx_q2_s1_in_target}}; October is recovering.
